title: Granularity from Sparse Spectrum
statement: Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. If the function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ obtained by encoding the sign cube coordinates as bits and evaluating $f$ has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Walsh Fourier coefficients, then every Fourier coefficient of $f$ is an integer multiple of $2^{-k}$.
hypotheses_covered: The encoded function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients
